wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking up the country's basics, and one that rises when Iran is at the centre of an unfolding story.
wiki-iran.recent: Attention has drained since the Hormuz standoff peaked in mid-July, falling roughly a third to its lowest reading on 13 August even as the confrontation continued: Trump claimed the US "owns" the Strait of Hormuz, US missiles crippled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, and the Guard Corps said it downed an MQ-9 Reaper near Bandar Abbas.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent has fallen roughly a fifth over the window, from $116.70 on May 18 to $93.26, with a low of $68.53 on Jul 2. The Strait of Hormuz has driven the recent trade: two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting it, and the US threatened an indefinite blockade of Iran — news that moved Brent 12 cents. The cost has landed instead on war-risk premia and pumps, with Pakistani diesel at 383.95 rupees a litre.

wti.standing: The US benchmark crude price, quoted at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the barrel most American refiners buy against. It moves on supply and policy, and gasoline, diesel and freight rates follow it down the chain.
wti.recent: Supply fear did the opposite of what the map suggests: WTI is down roughly a quarter over the window, from $112.30 on May 18 to $84.77, and traders have priced repeated strikes on production as a rounding error. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz, a third drone strike hit Libya's Zawiya refinery, and 12 missiles hit Yemen's oil provinces.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and used to price most American gas contracts. It sets what power plants, factories and heating bills pay, and it moves on weather, storage and how much gas is being shipped out as LNG.
natgas-hh.recent: The series has drifted down about 9% over the window, from $3.34 on May 29 to a low of $2.56 on Aug 7, without a clear cause in view. Demand-side commitments kept building: SpaceX said it would build its own natural gas power plants for a Texas chip factory, and Amazon backed a Fort Stockton plant of 35 turbines.

wheat.standing: The world price of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. Its level sets the cost of bread and flour across importing countries, and governments that subsidise the loaf carry the difference on their own budgets.
wheat.recent: Prices have risen through the summer as war and drought hit the supply chain at once: Russia set Izmail, Ukraine's largest Danube grain port, ablaze and struck its rail station, while drought across Europe ran the Danube low enough to shut a reactor at Cernavoda. The FAO's food price index reached 131.1.

rice.standing: The benchmark export price for a tonne of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the world's population. It is thinly traded relative to wheat or maize, so export bans by a single large supplier can move it sharply.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen against a wider food-price rise: the Food and Agriculture Organization's index hit 131.1, a three-year high driven by heatwaves and wars pushing up crop costs, while diesel at $5.36 a gallon added freight cost to other staples. A record El Nino threatens 49 million with acute hunger in southern Africa.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries current in every grid, motor and building wire. Demand tracks electrification and construction, and supply sits with a handful of mines, so the price reads as a gauge of how fast the world is wiring itself.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the benchmark price of borrowing for the world's largest borrower. It sets the floor under mortgages, corporate credit and sovereign spreads everywhere, and moves on inflation, Fed policy and demand for Treasuries.
us-10y.recent: The yield sat near the top of its range after the BOJ held rates at 1% on 31 July while warning underlying inflation was running above its 2% target, the same day the series peaked at 4.75%. Since then the dollar fell to its weakest since May as a rate hike came into doubt, and Trump again moved to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence.

sp500.standing: The main US stock index, tracking the 500 largest listed American companies. It is the reference return for most of the world's pension and reserve portfolios, so a move here is felt far beyond New York.
sp500.recent: The index sits near the top of its 62-day range, having risen roughly 5% from its 10 June low to a 13 August peak of 7,799. The AI trade drove the swing: Nvidia partnered with lenders to finance AI infrastructure, Palantir short sellers took a $3 billion hit after a 30% surge, and Jane Street took a $15 billion loss in July as AI stocks slumped.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by a handful of US technology firms, so it moves less with the broad economy than with the fortunes of chipmakers, cloud providers and phone makers.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its 62-day range after recovering from a Jul 29 low of 27,190, a 3.6% rise across the window that leaves it just short of the Jun 2 high of 30,660. The input does not identify what drove the turn.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump for a gallon of regular gasoline, tracked weekly by the EIA. It follows crude oil with a lag of a week or two, and it is the price through which distant supply shocks reach household budgets.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refineries have been the target rather than the wells: Ukrainian drones hit two Russian refineries on 6 August and killed 13 at Nizhnekamsk on 10 August, a third drone strike burned Libya's Zawiya refinery, and a fire hit an Aramco facility at Jizan. The pump price still sits near $4.01, down about a tenth over the window and above the $3.78 low of 6 July.

natgas-ttf.standing: The European benchmark price for natural gas, set at the Dutch TTF hub and the reference for most gas traded across the continent. It is what heating, electricity generation and fertiliser and chemical production are priced off, and industry contracts follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: The price sits well above its December low, and the pipeline politics behind European supply stayed live: Russia's envoy accused Germany of seeking a scapegoat over the Nord Stream attack and predicted only formal measures in response. Demand-side pressure is building elsewhere too, with SpaceX planning natural gas power plants for a Texas chip factory.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility traders expect in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days, priced off index options. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as the market's fear gauge.
vix.recent: The gauge has drifted down through the summer, from 22.22 on Jun 10 to 14.55 on Aug 12, its lowest of the period. The calm is not confined to equities: bitcoin volatility nearly vanished over the same stretch as ETFs took in $754 million, and traders read the sell-off from $65,000 as thin volume rather than panic.

fx-pkr.standing: Pakistan's currency against the US dollar. A country that imports its fuel, edible oil and much of its machinery pays for them in dollars, so the rupee's level sets the price of a litre of diesel and the size of the import bill.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat over the month, ranging between 278.2 on Jul 22 and 276.6 on Jul 31 and ending at 277.6 — steadiness that has not spared the import bill. Diesel now costs 383.95 rupees a litre after a war-risk levy tied to Hormuz, and Islamabad has asked Washington for $10 billion in dollars to shore up reserves.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. West Africa's largest economy runs on imported fuel, food and machinery, so the rate sets domestic prices, and oil exports are the main source of the dollars that back it.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira has been steady through a month of political rather than monetary news: the Osun election drew allegations of rigging and 34 violent incidents with 18 deaths before Saturday's vote, and an EFCC freeze on Osun's account was vacated on Tinubu's order. On the oil side, Abuja is forgoing tax to unlock $50 billion in deep offshore investment as output declines.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency, quoted as pounds per US dollar. A managed float in an economy that imports much of its food and medicine, so its level sets what an import-dependent household pays and what dollar-denominated debt costs to service.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has held near 50 to the dollar through the month, easing from 51.37 on 25 July to a low of 49.56 on 8 August. The earlier devaluation is still working through domestic prices: Cairo is weighing flexible drug pricing after a pricing freeze left pharmacy shelves empty, with importers unable to cover costs at the fixed rate.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira's exchange rate against the US dollar. Turkey runs persistent inflation and a large external financing need, so the rate is a live gauge of confidence in its monetary policy and of the cost of everything the country imports.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a 30-day low of 47.88 on Aug 14, roughly 1.5 percent weaker across the month, through a period dominated by Ankara's foreign policy rather than its economy: the Mecca defence pact signed with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on Aug 7, and the Kurdish disarmament law passed Aug 10. Nothing in the record ties either to the currency.

fx-bdt.standing: The exchange rate of Bangladesh's currency against the US dollar. It sets the import cost of fuel, food and industrial inputs for a country whose economy runs on garment exports, and it prices the remittances sent home by millions of workers abroad.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka strengthened from 124 on Aug 7 to 122.7 on Aug 15, its firmest level of the month. The available reporting on Bangladesh in this window covers Dhaka's approach to Delhi over ex-PM Hasina's planned speech and India's denial of involvement, and does not explain the currency's move.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. It prices Southeast Asia's largest economy, and Indonesia's imported fuel, food and dollar debt are settled through it.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah has firmed roughly two thirds of a percent over the month, from 18,110 on 28 July to 17,800 on 8 August and 17,830 now. The one currency story in the window is Prabowo's nomination of a Bank Indonesia deputy as the central bank's new governor on 11 August, on which the rupiah rose slightly.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. After the 2019 banking collapse the currency lost most of its value, and the rate now set by the central bank is the price at which salaries, imports and savings are measured for a country that buys nearly everything abroad.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has been effectively flat over the past month, moving less than a fifth of a percent between 89,180 on Jul 31 and 89,720 on Aug 7 — a peg holding steady rather than a market clearing. It has not moved with the war: Israeli strikes on Hula and south Lebanon, demolitions near Mansouri that registered magnitude 3.8, and a seventh round of direct talks in Rome all passed without a mark on the rate.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency, quoted as yuan per dollar, and the price at which the world's largest exporter's goods are converted into everyone else's money. Beijing manages it within a daily band, so its level is a policy signal as much as a market one.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan sat at its 30-day strongest against the dollar, drifting a few tenths of a percent firmer since mid-July with no single event behind it. Zhu Rongji, the premier who restructured China's state enterprises and steered WTO accession, died on 12 August; Washington accused Beijing of evading tariffs, and Beijing tightened drone exports.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar, quoted as rupees per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupee. India imports most of its crude, so the rate sets the domestic cost of fuel and of the dollar debt its companies carry.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has firmed about 0.9% over the past month, from 96.65 on 18 July to 95.05 on 5 August before easing to 95.45. Oil falling 4.5% on a remark about Iran cut the import bill that drives dollar demand. Retail inflation rose to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, with onion prices up 22.54%.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar — so a rising number means a weaker real. It prices Latin America's largest economy, and swings in it move the cost of the soy, beef, iron ore and coffee Brazil sells the world.
fx-brl.recent: The real slid to its weakest of the month against the dollar on Aug 15, capping a 2.1% decline from Jul 23. Washington revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador on Aug 4, saying it would restore it only if Brasília accepted its own envoy pick, and the Workers' Party nominated Lula for a fourth term two days earlier.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate of Mexico's peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. It is a standing proxy for the US-Mexico relationship, and it moves on trade policy, remittances and the rate gap between the two central banks.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso has firmed through the window, reaching its strongest level of the month on Aug 15 despite a steady run of friction with Washington: a $25 million bounty on a Mexican cartel leader, the fragmentation of the Sinaloa Cartel, and the revocation of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa, which Claudia Sheinbaum condemned. None of it dented the currency.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, the most traded currency pair in the world. It moves on the gap between what the European Central Bank and the Federal Reserve do with interest rates, and it sets the import price of energy and food for 350 million people.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted down about 1.1 percent over the month from its 26 July high to 0.8643 on 15 August. Nothing in the European news of the period explains it: the run of stories was regulatory and domestic — an EU sourcing law in draft, France's court striking down its under-15 social media ban, jellyfish shutting three nuclear reactors at Gravelines.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, the second-most traded in the world and the funding leg of the global carry trade. It moves on the gap between Japanese and foreign interest rates, and a cheap yen flatters exporters' earnings while raising the price of everything Japan imports.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen's strongest reading of the month, 156.5 on Aug 3, came with a joint US-Japan intervention that pushed the dollar to a one-month low — historic in that Washington took part at all. It has since given back part of that ground to 159.3. The cheap yen showed up in earnings a day later, when Toyota's quarterly profit reached $9.4 billion.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, and the cleanest daily read on how sanctions, oil revenue and war spending are landing on Russia's economy. A weaker ruble raises the cost of every import Russians still buy.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened through a fortnight in which Ukrainian strikes reached Russia's export and industrial interior: a drone attack on Nizhnekamsk killed 13 some 1,600 km from the Ukrainian border, the Baltic oil hub at Ust-Luga was hit, and drones burned nearly $2 billion of stock in Wildberries depots. Lavrov then rejected freezing the war at the current front line.

fx-zar.standing: The price of one US dollar in South African rand, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It carries the country's exposure to commodity prices and global risk appetite, so it moves on metal demand and foreign rate decisions as much as on domestic news.
fx-zar.recent: The rand has firmed steadily over the past month, from 16.83 on 25 July to a low of 16.15 on 8 August before settling at 16.17. The available material does not identify what drove the move.

btc.standing: The first cryptocurrency and the largest by market value, traded around the clock on exchanges worldwide. It is held both by individuals in self-custody wallets and, increasingly, by funds and corporate treasuries, which ties its price to conventional finance.
btc.recent: The Coldcard exploit set the tone: losses spread to 4,500 addresses and neared $89 million, and bitcoin slipped under $63,000 as holders sent coins back to exchanges. The attacker's own transactions congested the network. Bitcoin now sits 49% below its record, lagging a stock rally even as ETFs took in $754 million.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by market value, and the settlement layer for most stablecoins, tokenised assets and decentralised trading. Its price is a proxy for how much capital is willing to sit inside that system.
eth.recent: Ether moved little across the month, ending near the middle of a narrow band. Prices declined in early August as the Coldcard wallet exploit — eventually put at $120 million — entered a fifth day, then recovered as the sweeps receded. Bernstein warned that failure of the Clarity Act, which missed its pre-recess vote window in the Senate, could spark another selloff.

paxg.standing: A claim on a fixed weight of gold, priced per troy ounce, held as a store of value outside any government's balance sheet. It rises when investors doubt currencies, central banks or the durability of returns elsewhere.
paxg.recent: Gold rebounded toward a ten-week high as markets braced for US inflation data, with spot hitting $4,392 an ounce on Wednesday, and the series peaked at $4,404 on Aug 13. The metal's role as a reserve asset drew separate scrutiny that week when KPMG counted Tether's gold bars by hand for the stablecoin issuer's first audit.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A field of computer science building systems that perform tasks once requiring human judgement, and now the organising bet of the technology industry. What it can do sets what work it displaces, what it fabricates and what states try to govern.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership climbed through a fortnight of governance stories: all 193 UN states met in Geneva on AI rules, Anthropic extended watermarking to text Claude only edits, and Spotify moved to stop promoting AI-tagged artists. Underneath sat the labour question — AI now completes junior developers' starter tasks in San Francisco and New Delhi alike.

wiki-russia.standing: The Wikipedia article on Russia, and a daily count of how many people open it. Attention to a country's overview page rises when something happens there that sends readers looking for the basics — the size of it, who runs it, how it got here.
wiki-russia.recent: The peak on Aug 8 came amid the deepest strikes yet inside Russia: a Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk, 1,600 km from the Ukrainian border, killed 13 including a child, and drones burned nearly $2 billion of stock in Wildberries depots. Ukraine then hit the Novorossiysk naval base, and Putin threatened to seize cargo ships.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Wikipedia's article on Pakistan, a nuclear-armed country of some 250 million people, and one of the reference pages readers reach for when the region is in the news. Its daily readership rises with events rather than with any schedule.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The peak on 29 July sits well above the 25 July low, and the input does not explain that swing. What the window does carry is Pakistan's alignment: the Makkah pact signed with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on 7 August, now building a standing joint command, and a suicide attack on a peace rally in Swat on 2 August that killed 14.

wiki-china.standing: The daily count of people reading Wikipedia's article on China. Attention series like this one move when a country enters a story large enough to send ordinary readers looking for background, so the shape of the curve marks the days the news broke.
wiki-china.recent: The 13 August peak followed a week in which China ran through several stories at once: Zhu Rongji, the premier whose restructuring cost tens of millions of jobs and carried China into the WTO, died on 12 August at 97; Beijing's regulator cleared Apple's China-only AI model, built with Alibaba; and Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy east of Taiwan.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman through which a fifth of the world's traded oil leaves the Gulf. It is narrow, has no overland substitute at scale, and any interruption to it prices into crude, freight and war-risk insurance worldwide.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership followed the strait's closure and the bargaining over reopening it: Iran set six conditions and added a reparations clause as the 60-day deal window narrowed, while Trump declared "We own it" and Oman mediated talks Tehran called messages rather than negotiations. Transits fell by a third, and two ADNOC tankers were struck.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The most-read Wikipedia article about Bitcoin, tracked as daily pageviews. It measures public curiosity rather than price, and tends to move when the network, its custody tools or its regulation make news.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The window sits between two custody failures: a Coldcard hack that drained $120 million, whose own transactions then congested Bitcoin, and a firmware bug through which thieves stole $88 million, prompting a wallet maker in Toronto to destroy inventory. Attackers also drained Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia each day. It rises when the kingdom is at the centre of a story, and tracks general curiosity rather than markets or policy.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Three states signed a collective-defence pact at Mecca on Friday, and Egypt stayed out; the deal names no obligations and never states whose nuclear deterrent applies. Houthi missiles then hit Marib and Najran, wounding 11 including a 4-year-old, and Yemen said its forces struck a Saudi military site.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the sitting US president, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises and falls with whatever the presidency is doing, making it a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention Washington is holding.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Readership through early August tracked the Strait of Hormuz standoff — Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructure, then claimed the US fully controls the strait while Iran, Oman and US officials moved closer to a deal. Attention bottomed on Aug 1 and revived around the Ankara decoy flight, when Trump left hidden inside a catering truck.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking up the country at all, and one that rises when something there reaches an audience beyond those who follow it already.
wiki-india.recent: The peak on 6 August fell in a run of governance stories out of New Delhi: a US Senate bill threatening 100% tariffs on India, a caste count restarted after 1931, and heatwaves added to the disaster list on 4 August. Attention held into Modi's Independence Day pledge of eight chip plants and nuclear reactors.

wiki-israel.standing: Wikipedia's article on Israel, and how many people open it each day. Attention to a country page rises with the events that put it in front of readers, so the count works as a rough gauge of how widely a story has travelled beyond the region it happened in.
wiki-israel.recent: The peak on Aug 11 came as Venezuela restored consular ties with Israel after 17 years, the sharpest of a run of Latin American reversals that also saw Chile and Honduras return ambassadors and Colombia recognise Israeli sovereignty over the occupied Golan Heights. The same day, more than 500 attacks were recorded in the West Bank in a week.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily pageviews for the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are reading up on the country. Attention here tends to move with the war rather than with anything internal to the encyclopedia.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The month's peak came before the current run of strikes on infrastructure. Since then: Russia set Izmail, Ukraine's largest Danube grain port, ablaze and hit its rail station; war-risk premiums have priced ships out of calling at Odessa; and a Ukrainian drone strike on Nizhnekamsk, 1,600 km from the border, killed 13. Lavrov rejected freezing the war at today's contact line.

wiki-nigeria.standing: The Wikipedia page for Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer. Daily readership of a country's page tracks how much of the world is looking at it on any given day.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Nigeria's aviation system broke down in early August: airport unions struck in Lagos, barricades sealed Air Peace's terminals in two cities and airlines suspended flights as terminal access was restricted, while investigators in Asaba lost crash evidence to a return flight that overwrote the black box. In Osogbo, 34 incidents and 18 deaths were recorded before Saturday's vote.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed under a blockade: US missiles crippled a civilian cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on 11 August, two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting the strait, and Tehran has made reopening conditional, with 8 to 15 ships crossing daily against a June peak of 44. The cost has already reached Pakistan's pumps, where diesel is 383.95 rupees a litre.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits about a fifth below its 90-day baseline as Houthi fire spread from the shipping lane to the coast: a projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August, missiles and drones hit the port of Mokha on 9 August, and six sailors died in a Bab al-Mandeb strike reported 11 August. Maersk raised profit guidance to $6.5 billion on the rerouting.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic is essentially flat against its own 90-day baseline, and the swing from 263 vessels on Jun 22 to 170 on Jul 19 is not explained by the strait itself. The Hormuz closure has cut Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia, redrawing which cargoes reach Asian refineries rather than how many ships transit here.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic is running about 15% below its 90-day baseline, with the sharpest swing between a low of 28 vessels on Jul 10 and a high of 401 two days later. Typhoon Dolphin forced flight cancellations and evacuations in China on 9 August, and Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy east of Taiwan. Neither the storm nor the exercise is tied in the input to a specific day of the traffic swing.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits have run about 5% under their own 90-day baseline, with the window swinging from 83 vessels on Jul 13 to 22 on Jul 22 and 29 now. The input does not explain the swing; the drought reporting in this window covers Europe and the Danube, not the isthmus.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has thinned as the war reached the shipping lanes: drones struck the Turkish-operated Nadezhda near Novorossiysk, another killed a crewman on a coal-hauling tanker, and Ukraine hit the Novorossiysk naval base and port on 12 August. Turkey has since turned back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic sits near the low end of its own range, and the input does not explain why. The strait's shores have been busy for other reasons: Spain imposed reciprocal border checks on Italy, and roughly 72,000 people crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, a city of 84,000. Neither event touches vessel movement.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has drifted down through the summer, with the low of 126 vessels on Aug 3 falling in the same week a dinghy carrying about 160 people caught fire off Boulogne-sur-Mer and drew rescue craft into the strait. Nothing in the record explains the wider decline; seas have stayed calm, peaking at 0.9m.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic has fallen back through the window, from 123 vessels a day on Jul 31 to 83, and now runs 5.9% below its own 90-day baseline. Nothing in the record explains the drop: seas stayed moderate, with a 2.3-metre maximum wave height and no weather alert.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to nothing, in line with a Black Sea in which war risk now decides who sails. Strikes have closed Odessa's ports, with war-risk premiums pricing ships out of calling there, Russia hit the railway station at the Danube grain port of Izmail, and Ukrainian drones struck the Novorossiysk naval base. Putin has threatened to seize cargo ships.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits below its mid-June level after weeks of Houthi fire reaching Saudi soil: strikes wounded 11 civilians in Najran, a claimed attack on the Jazan refinery that processes 400,000 barrels of crude daily, and a fire Aramco says was extinguished at its Jizan facility. Riyadh signed the Mecca defence pact with Turkiye and Pakistan on 7 August but has not retaliated.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index has drifted down roughly 3% over two months, off its 14830 high on Jun 18. Turkey signed a mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in Mecca on 7 August and passed a Kurdish disarmament law on 10 August, while drones struck a Turkish-operated ship near Novorossiysk and Ankara began rationing Bosphorus passage.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz on 13 August, and Iran made new demands around the strait days earlier; seven blasts hit Jebel Ali port on 5 August. The index sits well below its 18 June high of 6270, with 137,000 Gulf tourism jobs forecast lost.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted down from its Aug 5 high of 1748 as the Hormuz closure reached Malaysian refineries, cutting Gulf crude arrivals to a fraction of normal volumes and forcing import substitution. Domestic politics added to the drag: Anwar Ibrahim's coalition lost Negeri Sembilan to a Malay-nationalist wave, and the DAP scheduled a vote on staying in the unity government.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has given up roughly 3% across the window, and the clearest domestic marker in that stretch was Prabowo's nomination of a central bank deputy as the new governor on 11 August, on which the rupiah rose slightly. The 1.6% single-day gain came alongside news that Indonesian warships had drilled with China's navy east of Taiwan.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Toyota's quarterly profit hit $9.4 billion, nearly doubling on a cheap yen — the clearest read on how much the currency has been worth to Japanese exporters. That prop was pulled on 3 August, when a joint US-Japan intervention pushed the dollar to a one-month low. The index has slipped from its 72,370 high on Jun 25.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits near the lower end of its range after a run of frictions between Beijing and Washington: the US accused China of evading tariffs, and Beijing tightened drone exports, setting up another trade clash. HSBC, a heavyweight in the index, launched a $1 billion share buyback after profits surged.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits about 6% below its mid-May peak of 4,178, having bottomed at 3,764 on 17 July before recovering to 3,927. Nothing in the period's China news explains the drift: the week's stories were Zhu Rongji's death at 97, Alibaba's open-model release, Apple's regulator-cleared China-only AI, and a fresh US accusation that Beijing is evading tariffs.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has fallen more than a tenth over the window, bottoming on Jul 30 before recovering. The memory trade drove both directions: SK Hynix dropped 5% on 7 August after approving $38B in new fabs, even as all 2027 memory capacity is already sold out and $880 billion rides on Korea's AI bet. North Korea fired a ballistic missile ahead of US-South Korea drills.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has gained about 15 percent over the past two months, reaching a high of 5,754 on Aug 11 before easing slightly. The input does not explain what drove the run.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits well above its 30 July low after a run driven by chip demand, though Taiwan's gains are narrow: chipmaking employs few of the island's workers, a two-speed economy Arizona is now trying to court beyond chips, pitching 100 Taiwanese investors on tax breaks and industrial parks. Security news ran the other way — Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy east of Taiwan, and AI agents extracted passwords over four days in a hacking campaign Taipei attributed last month.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits at its 45-day high after a 6.5% climb from the 19 May low, holding through a run of domestic shocks: the Nonthaburi school shooting on 7 August that killed eight and wounded 15, and Bangkok's reception of Min Aung Hlaing, which widened ASEAN fractures over Myanmar.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing off a late-May low, but slipped on the day. Manila's politics have run through the period: the Sara Duterte impeachment trial reached Day 14 with confidential-fund disbursements logged to unusual names and zero results, and a magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck the southern Philippines on 5 August.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the high it set on Aug 6, having climbed roughly a twentieth over the window, though it slipped on the latest session. The RBA held its cash rate steady on Aug 11 as the housing market softened, and China's steel stock has aged enough to recycle — a shift toward scrap that skips Australian iron ore, the index's largest export earner.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index sits at 114,100, roughly 2.8% below where it started the window. It peaked at 117,500 on Aug 7 and bottomed at 108,300 on Jul 23. Nothing in the available material explains the swing.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index sits at the bottom of its 66-day range after a summer of Brasília-Washington friction: Washington revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador on 4 August, tying its restoration to Brasília accepting its own envoy pick, and Lula was nominated for a fourth term two days earlier. Domestic rulemaking added to it, with Brazil imposing a 24-hour delay on crypto transfers above $10,000.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down through a run of US friction with Mexico City: Washington cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum, and offered $25 million for a Mexican cartel leader. A screwworm outbreak passing 500 human cases adds a hit to the livestock trade.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index has climbed roughly 7 percent over the window, reaching a high of 36,760 on Aug 13 before easing. The coverage from Canada in this period concerns wildfires in British Columbia, where 20,000 people were evacuated, and a WestJet flight attendants' strike — neither of which explains the move.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index climbed roughly 5% over the quarter, reaching 7799 on Aug 13, as the Strait of Hormuz standoff moved toward a deal rather than a war: Trump halted planned attacks on Iran's infrastructure on Aug 2 and talks involving Oman were reported making progress. It slipped 0.17% after the IRGC downed a US MQ-9 over Hormozgan.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 66-day range, having climbed from 10,200 in mid-May to a high of 10,910 on 29 July before easing back to 10,750. Domestic news has been political and regulatory rather than market-moving: Nigel Farage reclaimed his Clacton seat in a by-election, and Ofwat provisionally cleared £3.4bn in extra water bill rises.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index reached its highest level of the period on Aug 14, up roughly 8% since May. Bank shares had support from Commerzbank saying a tie-up with UniCredit could create value, a deal Berlin had previously called a sovereignty threat. Little else in the window points at Frankfurt directly.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index reached 8,726 on Aug 10 and has drifted since, ending at 8,637. The domestic news in the window was not market-moving: France's top court struck down the under-15 social media ban, and jellyfish swarms shut three nuclear reactors, knocking out 3.2 gigawatts. Nothing here explains the drift.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index climbed to a high of 1,120 on Aug 13, up about 9 percent over the past 67 days from a low of 1,010 on May 15, and slipped 0.16 percent on the latest session. The coverage from Amsterdam in this window is on cyberattacks and data residency rather than on the listed companies, and does not explain the move.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index reached 20,210 on 11 August, near the top of a run of roughly 13% since a 17,620 low on 15 May. Nothing in the Spanish news of the period explains the climb: the domestic stories were the Ceuta crossings, where 72,000 people entered a city of 84,000, and reciprocal border checks with Italy — neither of which touched the listed banks and utilities that dominate the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range, having climbed roughly 7% from its 19 May low of 48,360 to a 7 August high of 53,720. Nothing in the record explains the run: the Italian news of the period was Spain's reciprocal border checks, the resignation of three directors at the space agency, and Milan-based Bending Spoons buying Airtable for $1.28bn.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range, up about 9% over the window and roughly a fifth of a percent below the 14,630 high set on Aug 10, after a low of 13,220 on Jun 3. The available material does not explain what drove the climb.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after climbing roughly 8 percent from its 15 May low of 3036, peaking at 3327 on 5 Aug before easing. The coverage in this window does not explain the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-spain.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Spain — a country page whose traffic sits near a baseline until something draws the world's eye to Spanish territory, then jumps as readers arrive looking for context.
wiki-spain.recent: The 20 July peak came ahead of the first total solar eclipse to cross Europe in 30 years, whose path of totality ran over Spain — under two minutes at Burgos, 81 seconds at Teruel — before the August 12 event itself. Ceuta added a second draw: 72,000 people crossed into a city of 84,000.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A prediction market on whether the US Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate untouched at its September meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as the case for a cut or a hike strengthens.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract climbed from 39% on Aug 1 to 75% on Aug 15, and the input does not carry a Fed policy story that explains the shift. The month's Polymarket news was about the venue rather than the rate: JPMorgan cut the market's banking relationship, and a federal order required Kalshi to keep operating in New York after a state lawsuit.

wiki-turkey.standing: A count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on Turkey each day. It rises when the country enters a story large enough to send readers looking for the basics — a war on its border, a treaty, a domestic rupture.
wiki-turkey.recent: Readership tracked Turkey's move into two hard commitments. On 7 August Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Mecca joint defence pact, a bloc whose obligations and nuclear guarantee were left unwritten, and Egypt stayed out. Three days later Ankara passed the Kurdish disarmament law, which never names Abdullah Öcalan's release.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Vladimir Putin ceases to be Russia's leader before the end of 2026. Traders price it as a probability, so the number is a bet on the durability of one man's hold on power, not a forecast anyone has issued.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The contract has drifted down over the past month, from 10% in mid-July to 8%, as Moscow signalled it intends to keep fighting rather than settle: Lavrov rejected freezing the war at today's contact line, and Deputy Foreign Minister Galuzin ruled out a freeze days earlier. Ukrainian drones reaching Nizhnekamsk, 1,600 km inside Russia, have not moved it.

poly-will-2-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve cuts its policy rate twice during 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves whenever the odds of easing shift — and the Fed's rate sets the floor under mortgages, corporate borrowing and the dollar.
poly-will-2-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-2026.recent: The contract sits near the bottom of its range, at 4% after a low of 2% on Jul 17 and a high of 4% on Jul 27 — small absolute moves in a market pricing two cuts as unlikely. The clearest event in the window was Trump's renewed move to fire Fed governor Cook on Aug 7, reviving the fight over Fed independence.

poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran extend their 60-day negotiating window. It prices what traders will pay for diplomacy holding, so it falls when the two sides trade fire rather than terms.
poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.recent: The price collapsed from 75% on Aug 6 to 14% as the Gulf turned kinetic rather than diplomatic: US missiles crippled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, the Guard Corps says it downed a US MQ-9 Reaper over Bandar Abbas, and Trump said of the Strait of Hormuz, "We own it.

stocks:SPOT.standing: Shares in the Swedish streaming company that carries the largest share of the world's paid music listening, listed in New York. Its price tracks subscriber growth and the royalty terms it strikes with labels and artists.
stocks:SPOT.recent: Spotify said it will stop promoting artists tagged as AI-generated, a change to how the platform surfaces music on its service. The stock closed at $512.80, up from a low of $469 on Jul 23 and short of the $524 reached on Jul 29.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Apple's listed shares. The company sells iPhones, Macs and services at global scale, so the price carries both consumer hardware demand and the cost of the components — chips, memory, displays — that go into every device it ships.
stocks:AAPL.recent: The slide from the 28 July high of $340.10 to $302.30 on 12 August ran alongside a squeeze on component costs: TrendForce put DRAM at $145, up from $39, and iPhone 18 Pro BOM cost is estimated to be up by 40%. On 14 August China's regulator cleared Apple's home-grown AI model.

stocks:BABA.standing: Shares in Alibaba, the Chinese e-commerce and cloud group whose retail platforms and Qwen model family make it one of the main proxies for Chinese consumer demand and for China's domestic AI stack.
stocks:BABA.recent: The stock's climb tracked a run of AI announcements out of Hangzhou: Alibaba's Qwen team claimed a coding benchmark lead in early August, and the shares peaked at $132.30 on Aug 10, days before the release of a 27-billion-parameter open model. China's regulator also cleared Apple's home-grown AI model for the market.
